description:
Desktop client for openHPSDR Protocol 1/2 SDR radios.

A Rust/egui desktop client for openHPSDR Protocol 1 and Protocol 2 radios (Metis/Ozy-style and Hermes/Orion-style boards), using WDSP for DSP.

- Protocol 1 (Metis/Ozy) and Protocol 2 (Hermes/Orion) support, with standard openHPSDR UDP discovery
- Multiple simultaneous receivers, each with its own VFO, mode, filter width, and band memory
- Spectrum/waterfall display with adjustable dB range, palette, and Click-to-Tune (CTUN)
- SSB/CW/AM/FM/digital modes, per-mode/per-band filter width and mode memory
- Noise blanker (NB/NB2), noise reduction (NR/NR2/NNR), and SNB, independently switchable
- AGC with selectable Off/Long/Slow/Medium/Fast modes
- TX: mic audio through WDSP's TXA chain, ALC, TX power/SWR meter with per-band PA calibration, and a Tune button
- PureSignal (PA linearization/predistortion), on both Protocol 1 and Protocol 2
- rigctl (Hamlib-compatible), TCI (WebSocket), and CAT (Kenwood TS-2000 emulation) control servers
- Dual VFO (VFO A/B) with Split -- transmit on VFO B while receiving on VFO A
- Selectable RX output / TX input audio devices, independent of the OS default
- Per-radio settings persistence, keyed by the radio's MAC address
- FPGA firmware upload and static IP configuration
Licence
- hpsdr-rs is now GPL-3.0-or-later (was GPL-2.0-or-later), so it can include piHPSDR's Saturn code (below). The hpsdr-proto, hpsdr-controller and hpsdr-remote crates stay GPL-2.0-or-later.
ANAN G2 (Saturn) over XDMA — untested
- Running on a G2's own Raspberry Pi, hpsdr-rs can drive the FPGA directly through the XDMA driver (/dev/xdma0_*), without p2app, as piHPSDR does. Stop p2app first; the radio shows in Discover as a Saturn with XDMA as its interface. HPSDR_SATURN_DEBUG=1 logs set-up and the receive stream.
- Ported from piHPSDR's Saturn code (G8NJJ, N1GP, DL1YCF). Not yet tried on a G2 — reports welcome.
Receive
- APF: CW audio peak filter (button in CW modes; Type, Tune, Bandwidth and Gain in Settings → CW).
- Manual notches (TNF): right-click the spectrum or waterfall to add, resize or remove notches; they stay on their RF frequency and apply to every receiver.
- Auto AGC, as Thetis's: the AGC threshold follows the noise floor (Auto beside AGC Gain; offset in Settings → RX, +20 dB by default).
- AGC speed is chosen from a menu, like NB and NR.
- With AGC Off, the AGC Gain slider becomes Fixed Gain (-20 to +120 dB).
- Pan slider after Mute, per receiver. Mute is now kept across restarts.
- The SNR is shown inside the S-meter, S reading left and SNR right.
VFOs and tuning
- Lock for VFO A and VFO B, and Sync (VFO B follows VFO A). VFO A's Lock also holds the mode, as Thetis.
- Frequency keypad: Enter kHz, Enter MHz and a decimal point.
- The VFO step is remembered per mode; FM channel steps 6.25, 12.5 and 25 kHz. Audio and Mic gain read in percent.
Transmit
- TX Filter: use the RX filter (default) or its own Low/High edges.
- TX Profiles: save and choose named sets of mic gain, TX EQ, Speech Processor, CESSB and TX filter.
- Monitor TX Audio has its own Volume.
TCI and CAT
- TCI (requested by ThetisLink users): second receiver's audio/IQ asked for before it opens, rx_step_att_ex, vfo_swap_ex, app_ex, mon_enable/mon_volume, rx_mute/mute, cw_keyer_speed, rx_balance, tx_profiles_ex/tx_profile_ex/tx_filter_band_ex, lock/vfo_lock/vfo_sync_ex, rx_apf_enable/rx_nf_enable, agc_auto_ex.
- CAT PC reads and sets the TX power (as a percentage of the maximum), so e.g. an SPE Expert amplifier can set the drive.
Web client and hpsdr-remote
- A tap lands on the nearest kHz (10 Hz in CW); a slide steps kHz to kHz.
- Spectrum and Waterfall on/off buttons, and a bar to size them; in the compact layout the toolbar moves up with them. These and Mute are remembered.
- NB, NR and AGC as drop-downs; band edge markers; -/+ beside the frequency.
- With no password set, web clients can listen and tune but not transmit.
- Phone layout fixes: frequency labels no longer overlap; a scrolling page on short (landscape) screens.
- The page reloads and reconnects if the browser loses its WebGL context.
Controllers
- Front-panel controller tuning knobs have clicks/step (1-20), so a single VFO step is easy to hit. hpsdr-rs and hpsdr-remote alike.
- Compact layout: the DSP popup puts the AGC on its own line with the RX gain.
Platforms
- Raspberry Pi: draws with OpenGL by default (Vulkan flickered).
- Linux: presents without vsync, so a hidden Settings window can no longer freeze the app.
- Linux packages add a Ham Radio menu for hpsdr-rs and hpsdr-remote (including on Raspberry Pi OS).
- Windows: all windows' title bars follow the dark/light theme (thanks K7MDL2, PR #19).
- Settings → Audio shows the device actually in use, and warns when the saved one is missing (issue #18).
- The FFTW wisdom file is saved inside its wdsp_wisdom folder (an existing misplaced one is moved there).
Documentation
- Manual updated for all of the above, with new and retaken screenshots.
